answer: An agent market requires each identity to lock a $100 bond for 30 days to receive one daily job slot. At each daily pulse, agents such as willow and quill can claim only their bonded quota. Creating 1,000 fake identities therefore ties up $100,000 for a month; splitting the same funds among more names buys no extra slots. The defense makes access depend on committed capital, so an attacker pays financing costs even if every bond is eventually returned.
